formCues: Drive the bar up explosively off the shoulders
Punch under the bar into a split or squat receive
Keep the bar path close and vertical
Lock out arms overhead before standing tall
Brace hard through the torso on the dip
setup: Start with the barbell racked across the front shoulders in a shoulder-width stance, elbows high and core braced.
commonMistakes: Pressing the bar with the arms instead of driving with the legs
Receiving the bar with an unstable front foot
Leaning back excessively on the drive
Failing to fully lock out overhead before recovery

formCues: Glide the head straight back, not down
Keep eyes level and jaw relaxed
Hold the retracted position briefly
Avoid shrugging the shoulders
setup: Sit or stand tall with a neutral spine and shoulders relaxed down and back.
commonMistakes: Tilting the chin down instead of retracting straight back
Tensing the shoulders during the movement
Moving too fast to feel the deep neck flexor engagement

formCues: Rack both kettlebells against the shoulders
Keep elbows up and torso upright
Sit hips back and down between the knees
Drive through the mid-foot to stand
Keep knees tracking over the toes
setup: Clean two kettlebells to a front rack position at the shoulders with feet shoulder-width apart.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows drop, causing the torso to fold forward
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Rising onto the toes on the way up
Allowing knees to cave inward

formCues: Distribute the load evenly across the shoulders and back
Brace the core before walking
Take controlled, stable steps
Keep the chest up and gaze forward
setup: Position the load (person, sandbag, or log) balanced across the upper back and shoulders with a secure grip on both sides.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine under the load
Rushing the lift into the carry position
Walking with an unstable, uneven gait
Failing to brace the core before moving

formCues: Land softly on the balls of the feet
Sweep arms fully overhead in sync with the leg jump
Keep a slight bend in the knees on landing
Maintain a quick, rhythmic pace
setup: Stand tall with feet together and arms relaxed at the sides.
commonMistakes: Landing flat-footed or stiff-legged
Letting arms and legs fall out of sync
Slouching the torso forward during the movement

formCues: Push the hips straight back to initiate
Keep the kettlebell close to the legs
Maintain a flat back throughout
Feel a stretch in the hamstrings before reversing
Drive hips forward to stand tall
setup: Hold a kettlebell with both hands in front of the thighs, feet hip-width apart and knees softly bent.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees too much and turning it into a squat
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Letting the kettlebell drift away from the body
Hyperextending the back at the top

formCues: Hold the sleeve close to the chest with both hands
Sit the hips back and down
Keep the chest tall and elbows in
Drive through the whole foot to stand
setup: Stand facing a landmine attachment, gripping the end of the barbell sleeve at chest height with both hands.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the chest
Rounding the upper back
Shifting weight onto the toes
Not reaching adequate squat depth

formCues: Turn the head roughly 45 degrees to one side
Gently tilt the chin toward the armpit
Use light hand pressure only, no yanking
Keep the opposite shoulder pressed down and relaxed
setup: Sit or stand tall, then rotate the head 45 degrees away from the side being stretched before tilting downward.
commonMistakes: Pulling too aggressively with the hand
Shrugging the shoulder on the stretched side
Rotating the head the wrong direction, missing the muscle

formCues: Plant the pole at an angle behind the body
Push off through the pole with each stride
Swing arms in opposition to the legs
Keep an upright, relaxed posture
setup: Stand holding a Nordic walking pole in each hand with a relaxed grip, ready to begin a walking stride.
commonMistakes: Planting the poles too far forward instead of behind
Gripping the poles too tightly
Not engaging the arms and core for propulsion
Taking overly short, shuffling steps

formCues: Balance on one leg with the other held behind
Sit the hips back and down under control
Keep the working knee tracking over the toes
Tap the rear knee lightly to the floor
Drive through the standing heel to rise
setup: Stand on one leg with the other leg lifted behind the body, arms extended forward for balance.
commonMistakes: Letting the standing knee collapse inward
Slamming the rear knee into the floor
Losing balance and touching down with the back foot
Leaning too far forward through the torso

formCues: Keep a low, athletic stance on the board
Engage the core to stabilize against the wave
Distribute weight evenly between both feet
Keep eyes up and focused ahead
setup: Position the body prone or standing on the surfboard with feet or hands placed for balance as a wave approaches.
commonMistakes: Standing up with too high a center of gravity
Looking down at the feet instead of ahead
Tensing up instead of flexing with the wave's motion
Poor foot placement leading to loss of balance

formCues: Keep the forearm supported and still
Move only at the wrist, lifting the thumb side up
Control the return to the starting position
Use a light load or no load initially
setup: Rest the forearm on a table or thigh with the hand hanging off the edge in a neutral thumb-up position.
commonMistakes: Moving the forearm or elbow to assist the lift
Using excessive weight that limits range of motion
Jerking the movement instead of controlling it

formCues: Keep the forearm supported and still
Move only at the wrist, lifting the pinky side up
Control the return to the starting position
Use a light load or no load initially
setup: Rest the forearm on a table or thigh with the hand hanging off the edge in a neutral thumb-up position.
commonMistakes: Moving the forearm or elbow to assist the lift
Using excessive weight that limits range of motion
Jerking the movement instead of controlling it
